scenario.name: Broad post-compromise host survey with local result staging
scenario.description: Run Seatbelt's all group to enumerate host, security-control, account, process, network, file, credential-opportunity, browser, token, and scheduled-task context, then stage the survey in a local JSON file.

sensors.name: Sysmon
sensors.config_notes: Verification-grade unfiltered process, network, DNS, file, and registry coverage; LSASS ProcessAccess EID 10 enabled.

collector.pktmon_reason: The scenario was local host enumeration. Sysmon recorded the only loopback connection and localhost DNS query, so a packet capture would not add useful detection evidence.

acquisition.build_tool: Microsoft Visual Studio Build Tools 2022 / MSBuild 17.14.51+25f168cee
acquisition.build_notes: The upstream project requests .NET Framework 3.5, whose legacy reference pack is not included with current Build Tools. The exact source was compiled unchanged with a command-line v4.7.2 target override using Microsoft's installed reference assemblies.
acquisition.transfer_notes: lab-push was attempted but failed because the helper invokes bash, which is absent in the Windows guest. The archive was transferred in bounded chunks through lab-exec over QEMU guest agent; the reassembled SHA-256 matched. Telemetry was retrieved with lab-pull after in-guest compression.

observed_techniques.name: System Information Discovery
observed_techniques.observation: The all group invoked OS, hotfix, runtime, environment, and system configuration checks.

observed_techniques.name: Software Discovery: Security Software Discovery
observed_techniques.observation: The all group invoked AntiVirus, WindowsDefender, Sysmon, AMSIProviders, and firewall checks.

observed_techniques.name: Query Registry
observed_techniques.observation: The scenario invoked registry-backed configuration checks. Sysmon exposed 37 Seatbelt-attributed write-class registry events but does not log the broader reads.

observed_techniques.name: Account Discovery: Local Account
observed_techniques.observation: The all group invoked LocalUsers and LocalGroups.

observed_techniques.name: System Owner/User Discovery
observed_techniques.observation: The all group invoked session, process-owner, token-group, and token-privilege checks.

observed_techniques.name: Process Discovery
observed_techniques.observation: The all group invoked Processes and InterestingProcesses; Sysmon also recorded two Seatbelt-to-LSASS ProcessAccess events.

observed_techniques.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
observed_techniques.observation: The all group invoked ARP, DNS, network-profile, share, and connection checks; Sysmon recorded loopback RPC and localhost resolution.

observed_techniques.name: File and Directory Discovery
observed_techniques.observation: The all group invoked directory, interesting-file, browser-presence, and credential-file checks.

observed_techniques.name: Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
observed_techniques.observation: The all group invoked CloudCredentials, WindowsCredentialFiles, DPAPI master-key, and application configuration checks. No result content was inspected.

observed_techniques.name: Credentials from Password Stores
observed_techniques.observation: The all group invoked WindowsVault, CredEnum, saved RDP, and Wi-Fi profile checks. No result content was inspected.

observed_techniques.name: Browser Bookmark Discovery
observed_techniques.observation: The all group invoked ChromiumBookmarks and browser history checks.

observed_techniques.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
observed_techniques.observation: The all group invoked the ScheduledTasks check to identify non-Microsoft task opportunities.

observed_techniques.name: Data Staged: Local Data Staging
observed_techniques.observation: Seatbelt created C:\lab\seatbelt-run.json through its outputfile argument.

network.assessment: Seatbelt initiated loopback TCP to 127.0.0.1:135 and resolved localhost. Both are generic local RPC/enumeration behavior, so no standalone Sigma rule was authored.

files.assessment: EID 11 recorded creation of the explicit C:\lab\seatbelt-run.json output. No file deletion was observed.

registry.assessment: Sysmon recorded CreateKey and SetValue-class activity attributed to Seatbelt. These events do not expose the broad read activity, and the targets were too generic for a standalone rule.

process_identity.assessment: Sysmon captured Image, OriginalFileName, path, hashes, System integrity, and the characteristic all-group command line.

parent_child.assessment: The Seatbelt EID 1 recorded powershell.exe as ParentImage and the wrapper invocation in ParentCommandLine.

additional_process_access.assessment: Seatbelt accessed LSASS with 0x1000 and 0x1410; the latter included a managed .NET System.ni.dll call trace.

evidence.description: Sanitized process identity, command line, working directory, and parent-child fields from the Seatbelt process creation event.
Sanitized network and file events plus registry counts and representative target objects for the five-dimension assessment.
Two sanitized Seatbelt-to-LSASS ProcessAccess events, including the managed .NET call trace used by Tier 2.

sigma.description: Primary portable, name-agnostic detection for -group= syntax or at least two distinctive Seatbelt check names; the repaired condition explicitly enumerates every pair of seven checks.

precision_measurement.verdict_reason: The positive corpus contains no managed .NET 0x1410 LSASS access sample; this is non-blocking and does not establish recall.
precision_measurement.measurement_provenance: VM 107 audit harness against the corrected category-only query and the catalog denominator in audit/catalog/baseline-category-metrics.json

previous_precision_measurement.reason: The rule declared category=process_access, product=windows, and service=sysmon. The THOR mapping selected category+product and rewrote service, leaving a compiling query that matched no events. The recorded zero was a null, not precision evidence.

recall_measurement.retained_evidence: evidence/sysmon-seatbelt-lsass-process-access.json records 0x1410 access to LSASS with both managed CallTrace substrings, but sanitized JSON is qualitative evidence and is not replayed by the EVTX harness.
recall_measurement.required_to_measure: Add a replayable positive EVTX sample, or repeat Seatbelt.exe -group=all -q on VM 104 from win_verify_baseline and grade the corrected rule against its EID 10 output. No target run was performed for this fix.

sigma.description: Deep Sysmon-native, name-agnostic detection for managed .NET access to LSASS with VM-read rights.

validation.pysigma: Both remaining Sigma rules passed sigma-cli 3.1.0 / pySigma validation on audit VM 107 on 2026-08-16.

sanitization.notes: The Seatbelt JSON survey was never inspected or pulled. Raw collector output was used transiently for analysis and excluded from the repository. The committed evidence contains selected telemetry fields only; the long lab wrapper in ParentCommandLine is summarized.
